central_question: Why does work-time often explain affordability better than converted prices?

verified_claims.claim: Work-time comparisons translate price into local labor burden, but results depend on wage definitions, tax assumptions, working hours and selected product price.
Raw dollar comparisons can obscure lived affordability because local wages and prices move differently.
Lifestyle bundles such as date-night comparisons can be readable but are context-sensitive and method-dependent.

useful_numbers_or_examples: hours of work to buy a phone
minutes of work to buy a burger
affordability as time rather than sticker price
myth_or_uncertainty_notes: Do not make current city rankings unless refreshed.
Use work-time examples to explain method, not to crown winners.
